title: Sharky's later playing and playing by mood
summary: Sharky relying on humor, his lip trouble, and how you feel on any day.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: That's so funny. Well Sharky was a funny man. Oh yeah. To be honest, it seemed to me as the years went on, Sharky relied more and more on his humor and his dancing and everything. I wanted to be able to... On the floor, on the stage while he was entertaining. On the stage, yeah. He really could put things over that way. And I wondered if he was having lip trouble towards the end. I would never say anything. Not one particle. He could still do it up to the end. I know.
Yeah, up till the time that he took sick.
Yeah. I know that some nights he played harder than others. And when he wanted to, he could still go.
Well, it all gets back to the same thing that I was just telling you. It's just how you feel that day.
And you can't name it what day. No. It's how you feel that day. The minute you sit down to play the first tune, you may feel like a million dollars or you may feel like a skunk.
Well, I'll tell you the truth from the beginning though. Those early records of Sharky. Maybe the Brownleys, he's not in top form for some reason. Honey! Oh.
